header.running_head: The Sahabah (RA) Weep at the Mention of Rasulullaah ﷺ Separating from them

blocks.text: understood the message of this statement besides Abu Bakr (RA). His eyes therefore filled with tears and he started weeping. He then exclaimed, 'May my parents be sacrificed for you, O Rasulullaah ﷺ! In fact, may all our fathers, our mothers, ourselves and our wealth be sacrificed for you!' Rasulullaah ﷺ then descended from the pulpit and has not stood there again to this day."[^1]
Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ sent for Hadhrat Faatima (RA) after Allaah revealed the Surah:

He said to her, "This tells me of my pending death." When she started to weep, Rasulullaah ﷺ consoled her by saying, "Do not weep because you shall be the first of my family to meet me." She then started to laugh. Seeing her do this, one of Rasulullaah ﷺ's wives asked, "I saw you cry and then laugh?" Hadhrat Faatima (RA) explained, "Rasulullaah ﷺ said to me, 'This tells me of my pending death.' When I started to weep, Rasulullaah ﷺ then consoled me by saying, "Do not weep because you shall be the first of my family to meet me." It was then that I started to laugh."[^2]

Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates, "During his final illness, Rasulullaah ﷺ once called for his daughter Faatima (RA). When he whispered something to her, she wept. He then called her again and when he whispered something to her this time, she started laughing. When I asked her about this, she replied, 'When Rasulullaah ﷺ informed me that his life would be taken during this illness, I started to weep but when he told me that I would be the first of his family to meet him, I started to laugh.'"[^3]

In another narration, Hadhrat Ummu Salamah (RA) states, "When I asked Faatima (RA) about her laughing and crying, she replied, 'Rasulullaah ﷺ first informed me that he was going to pass away and then informed me that I would be the leader of the women of Jannah after Maryam the daughter of Imraan (AS). It was this that made me laugh.'"[^4]

Hadhrat Alaa (RA) reports that when Rasulullaah ﷺ was about to leave this world, Hadhrat Faatima (RA) started weeping. Rasulullaah ﷺ said to her, "Do not weep, dear daughter. When I pass on, you should say, 'Innaa Lillaahi wa Innaa Ilayhi Raaji'oon' because by reciting these words a person receives something in return for every calamity." "Even in return for losing you, O Rasulullaah ﷺ!" asked Hadhrat Faatima (RA). "Even in return for losing me," replied Rasulullaah ﷺ.[^5]
Ibn Abi Shaybah, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.4 Pg.58). Ibn Sa'd (Vol.2 Pg.230) has reported a similar narration from Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri (RA).
Tabraani. Haythami (Vol.9 Pg.23) has commented on the chain of narrators.
Ibn Sa'd (Vol.2 Pg.247). Ibn Sa'd has also reported the narration in greater detail.
